Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q2 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Barnes, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Barnes, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech’s earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Johnson, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; and Sarah Lee, COO.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Alex Johnson.

Alex Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

We made strong progress this quarter. Our revenue and gross margin guidance for the third quarter of fiscal year 2024, ending September 30, 2024, anticipates revenue to land between USD 19.6 billion and USD 20.4 billion. This reflects a growth trajectory that, while solid, is tempered by ongoing macroeconomic uncertainties and strategic shifts within key market segments. We project gross margin to be in the range of 51% to 53%, a reflection of optimized supply chain management, a favorable product mix shift towards higher-margin offerings, and continued efforts in manufacturing efficiency.

We also saw great momentum in our inventory management. As previously communicated, our Days of Inventory (DOI) increased by 5 days this quarter, reaching 90 days, compared to 85 days in Q2 2024 and 78 days in Q3 2023. While this increase warrants close attention, it is largely attributed to our strategic ramp-up of production for our next-generation 3-nanometer (3nm) technologies. This ramp-up represents a significant investment in future growth and market leadership, and the inventory build is considered a necessary, albeit temporary, effect.

These achievements underscore our commitment to disciplined execution and innovation.

Now I’ll pass it to Michael Chen to walk through in more detail.

Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Alex, and hello, everyone.

Let me take you through the financials:

First, building on what Alex said, we’ve continued to drive improvements in inventory management. The primary driver behind the DOI increase is the planned accumulation of both raw materials and work-in-progress (WIP) inventory related to 3nm. 3nm technology utilizes exotic and highly specialized materials with longer lead times and higher costs compared to our legacy processes. To ensure a smooth production start and avoid potential supply chain bottlenecks, we proactively increased our stock of these critical materials, contributing approximately 40% to the overall DOI increase. We saw a 30% increase in raw materials inventory specifically related to 3nm compared to the previous quarter, representing an investment of roughly $125 million. As we bring 3nm fabrication lines online, the initial yield rates are naturally lower than our mature processes. This requires a larger WIP inventory buffer to ensure we meet our committed delivery schedules to key customers. The WIP inventory specifically related to 3nm accounted for approximately 50% of the DOI increase. A smaller portion (approximately 10%) of the DOI increase is a deliberate strategic buffer against ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty and potential disruptions in global supply chains.

We invested strategically in this area, resulting in a solid operating margin performance for the third quarter of 2024. Our operating margin increased by 0.4 percentage points sequentially to 42.0%, a figure we believe reflects a successful execution of our strategic initiatives and favorable market dynamics. We experienced a 7% increase in revenue quarter-over-quarter, reaching $2.41 billion in Q3 compared to $2.25 billion in Q2. This top-line growth allowed us to leverage our fixed operating costs more effectively. Our supply chain optimization program, “Project Streamline,” began to yield tangible results in Q3. We successfully negotiated more favorable terms with key suppliers of raw materials for our core product lines, resulting in a 2.5% reduction in the cost of goods sold (COGS) on a per-unit basis. We implemented a more targeted marketing strategy, focusing on high-ROI channels and leveraging data analytics to personalize campaigns. This resulted in a 5% decrease in marketing expenses as a percentage of revenue compared to Q2. While inflationary pressures persist, our proactive hedging strategies and pricing adjustments mitigated the impact on our operating margin.

Additionally, we’ve seen progress in our capital expenditure strategy, and we believe our capital budget for the full year 2024 is projected to fall within a range of USD 28 billion to USD 32 billion. We are maintaining this range despite some fluctuations in market demand we observed in Q2 and early Q3, reaffirming our commitment to long-term growth and technological leadership. We are dedicating 70-80% of our CapEx to advanced process technologies and 10-20% to specialty technologies.

Now I’ll turn it over to Sarah, who will speak about operations and innovation.

Sarah Lee, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Michael.

Let me begin with a closer look at the P&L guidance, particularly on the revenue breakdown. At the lower end of the revenue guidance ($19.6 billion), we are factoring in a potential slowdown in consumer spending due to inflationary pressures, particularly in the North American and European markets. This scenario assumes a more conservative growth rate in our consumer electronics division, specifically for premium television sets and high-end audio equipment. Furthermore, the lower end incorporates the possibility of delayed contract renewals within our enterprise software solutions, stemming from protracted budget approval cycles amongst our larger clients. Conversely, the upper end of the revenue guidance ($20.4 billion) assumes continued strong performance in our cloud services segment, driven by a robust uptake of our AI-powered analytics platform. We anticipate a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion within this segment, fuelled by key customer wins in the healthcare and financial services industries. This optimistic scenario also anticipates a successful launch of our new AI-accelerated hardware line, specifically targeting the burgeoning market for edge computing solutions. Early pre-order data suggests significant demand, particularly from telecommunications providers and manufacturing firms seeking to optimize their operational efficiency.

I’d also like to expand on our gross margin results. Our first quarter gross margin landed at 53.1%, a slight but positive increase of 0.1 percentage points sequentially from Q4 2023's 53.0%. This improvement reflects the resilience of our operational strategies. The primary driver of this sequential uptick was a favorable product mix shift, directly attributable to the seasonality of our smartphone business. We witnessed a higher proportion of sales in our higher-margin premium smartphone models during Q1. This positive product mix effect was partially offset by less favorable foreign exchange rates. The strengthening US dollar eroded our gross margin by an estimated 0.5 percentage points. Compared to Q1 2023, the gross margin of 53.1% represents a stable performance. For the second quarter of 2024, we are guiding for a gross margin of 52.0% at the midpoint, representing a decline of 1.1 percentage points sequentially from Q1 2024. This anticipated decrease is primarily driven by the earthquake in Taiwan on April 3rd and higher electricity costs in Taiwan.

Let’s move to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
You mentioned strong improvements in operating margin. Can you talk more about the drivers for the year-over-year increase?

Michael Chen:
Certainly. We saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.41 billion, driven by robust demand for our cloud-based solutions and the successful expansion into new geographic markets. Our higher-margin software and services segments continued to represent a larger portion of our overall revenue mix. The shift towards these segments, which have inherently higher operating margins, contributed significantly to the year-over-year improvement. Furthermore, we continue to drive efficiency in our R&D spending. The integration of “Innovate Solutions,” acquired in Q4 2023, is progressing ahead of schedule, realizing significant cost synergies.

Analyst 2:
Can you elaborate on the trajectory of Days of Inventory and the mitigation strategies you plan to implement?

Sarah Lee:
Sure. We anticipate that DOI will remain elevated in Q4 2024 as we continue to ramp up 3nm production. However, we expect DOI to begin to decline in the first half of 2025 as yield rates improve and our inventory optimization initiatives take effect. We are committed to managing our inventory levels prudently and efficiently to maximize shareholder value. We expect that the Q1 2025 DOI will lower approximately 3 days to 87 days. To mitigate the impact of the elevated DOI and improve inventory efficiency, we are implementing several key strategies, including yield enhancement programs for 3nm, investing in more sophisticated demand forecasting tools, implementing advanced inventory optimization techniques, and carefully phasing our 3nm capacity expansion to match the pace of demand growth.

Analyst 3:
With regard to CapEx guidance, how does the increasing geopolitical tensions impact your investment strategy?

Michael Chen:
Increased geopolitical tensions have accelerated the trend of regionalizing semiconductor manufacturing. This has led us to expedite our investments in our facilities in the United States and Europe, as we seek to diversify our manufacturing footprint and reduce our reliance on any single region. This includes accelerating our Fab 21 expansion in Arizona and solidifying our plans for Fab 38 in Germany.

Closing

Alex Johnson:
Thank you all for joining us today. We're energized by the momentum we’re seeing and look forward to sharing continued progress next quarter.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
